concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: Before the amendment became effective on 1 October 2026, the DPA required notification no later than 48 hours after the Processor became aware of a breach.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment effective from 1 October 2026 replaced the 48-hour deadline with a requirement to notify the Controller no later than 24 hours after awareness.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the prior written notice period for routine on-site audits from 30 days to 20 days. The amendment's main body prevails over the annex audit protocol.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment replaced the prior fee-based liability formula with an aggregate Processor liability cap of EUR 1,000,000.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability provision expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd remained an approved Sub-processor on 1 November 2026 because its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The amendment withdrew Meridian Mail Ltd's approval with effect from 1 January 2027, so it was no longer approved on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, Personal Data was stored or processed in Norway, Estonia, Ireland, Lithuania, France, and Denmark, yielding six distinct countries.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: For a termination on 31 December 2026, the amended 60-day deletion or return period expires on 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: as of 1 november 2026, the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notice must include the required breach details, and the processor must document the breach and cooperate with related regulatory or data-subject communications.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: As of 1 November 2026, the Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notice must include the required breach details, and the Processor must document the breach and cooperate with related regulatory or data-subject communications.
justifications: The amended breach provision imposes a 24-hour outer deadline while preserving the separate duty to notify without undue delay and the existing notification-content and cooperation requirements.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach involved confirmed exposure of usable privileged credentials, which triggers the expedited 12-hour initial-notification limit.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April, making the 12-hour outer limit 05:10 on 10 April; notice was delivered at 06:00, 50 minutes late.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The third Business Day after awareness is 16 April: 13 April is the first counted day, 14 April is excluded under the approved pause, and 15 and 16 April are the second and third counted days.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 29 August 2027, while the final legal hold ends on 25 August and the tenth Business Day afterward is 9 September. The later date therefore governs deletion.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup's ordinary deletion deadline is 29 August 2027, but 35 calendar days after its 30 June creation is 4 August. The earlier date applies, and the later restore does not restart the period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation and not for service delivery or analytics. The applicable hold remains in force on 1 September 2027 because the deletion deadline is 9 September.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Authorisation begins on the latest of the proposed start date, completed security review, and written Controller consent. The security review and actual processing both occurred on 22 April 2027, later than the other conditions.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS continues ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd is withdrawn for ordinary email, and the Finland proposal lacks consent and has not begun processing.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: Actual processing with effective authorisation is established in Estonia, France, Lithuania, Norway, and Sweden as of 15 May 2027. Denmark is withdrawn, Ireland is covered only by an expired emergency interval, and Finland and Germany lack the required processing and/or authorisation.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the service credit, one-off training, and the event month's fees. Twice that amount, EUR 2,280,000, exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 floor and therefore sets the security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000, and EUR 300,000 has already been paid for ordinary breaches in the same Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary claim is payable up to the EUR 700,000 remaining ordinary pool; the shared security loss is payable at EUR 1,750,000; and the two confidentiality-priority losses are payable at EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000. Together, the new claims total EUR 2,800,000.
